title: Preserve per-series FRED freshness in compact live anchors
objective: Repair the compact live-anchor macro embedding so each FRED series preserves deterministic source-timestamp and freshness/health semantics already produced by the FRED owner. A stale slow-frequency observation may remain available as context but must not be indistinguishable from a fresh observation. Implement the smallest owner-consumer lineage repair without changing FRED cadence, source selection, stale thresholds, market interpretation, or API budget.
allowed_change_scope: scripts/data_terminal/fred_multiseries_live_adapter.py only if required to expose already-existing owner metadata deterministically
tests/daily_capture/directly related live-anchor macro freshness tests
tests/data_terminal/directly related FRED adapter contract tests

evidence.summary: The FRED owner already computes per-series source_timestamp, retrieval_timestamp, freshness_seconds, stale_after_seconds and PASS/STALE using the existing seven-day stale policy.
latest_fred_values() rereads raw CSV payloads and emits only {value,date}; it does not consume or preserve the owner's per-series source health/freshness fields.

The compact anchor embeds DTWEXBGS date 2026-08-21 value 118.0628 alongside fresher DGS/VIX values but carries no per-series freshness/status, so downstream cannot distinguish latest-available from fresh.
FRED macro is intentionally collected once per day on source-appropriate cadence; the fix must preserve this cadence rather than recollecting slow data more frequently.

reproduction: On fresh main, inspect fred_csv_collector.build_artifacts() and confirm source_health rows carry per-series status/freshness. Then inspect build_capture_index.latest_fred_values() and a morning live-anchor capture. Confirm the compact market_metrics.macro entries contain only date/value and omit the already-known owner freshness/status fields. If current main already preserves equivalent deterministic per-series freshness in the compact anchor, stop as clean no-op.

positive: A fixture with DGS2/DGS10/VIX within freshness policy and DTWEXBGS older than stale_after_seconds produces a compact anchor where the three fresh series remain PASS and DTWEXBGS is explicitly STALE.
Each embedded macro series carries source_timestamp or equivalent source date, retrieval_timestamp, freshness_seconds, stale_after_seconds and status sufficient for downstream quality-aware use.
Latest-available stale data remain numerically available as context while their stale status is preserved; no consumer must infer freshness from presence alone.
The compact anchor remains deterministic and source lineage/readback tests pass without increasing source calls.
negative: Do not change DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS or introduce a new market/freshness threshold.
Do not change the FRED collection schedule, add API calls, switch provider, or increase API budget.
Do not convert STALE to bearish, zero, missing, or a market-state vote.
Do not forward-fill, interpolate, fabricate a newer source date, or retrospectively rewrite historical captures.
Do not make macro evidence binding or alter canonical market/portfolio authority.

clean_noop_condition: Fresh main already preserves deterministic per-series FRED freshness/status in the compact live-anchor market_metrics.macro surface.
stop_condition: Stop without code changes if the compact anchor is not a downstream decision/calibration input or if equivalent freshness lineage is already preserved through a canonical adjacent field consumed by all readers.
escalation_condition: Escalate only if preserving existing owner health would require a breaking compact-anchor contract change rather than a backward-compatible field extension.
